Cliopatria draws no Portuguese shape before 1640; its 1640 shape in the Grao-Para region (204,000 km2, to 1.9 N) is carried back to 1621.

ledger.note: 1621 (13 June): Philip II of Portugal creates the State of Maranhao. 'The state was created on 13 June 1621 by Philip II of Portugal'; it was based at Sao Luis and 'encompassed a large part of the Amazon rainforest' (captaincies Maranhao, Para, Ceara).

region.text: the 221 Maranhão cells of Cliopatria's New Netherland 1642 shape: the captaincy of Maranhão with São Luís

ledger.note: 1641: the Dutch take the captaincy of Maranhão. 'In 1641, the Dutch captured the captaincy of Maranhão' (Dutch Brazil page); 'by 1641, the Dutch captured São Luís' (Dutch–Portuguese War page). Mirrors dutch-brazil /ledger/4, which books the gain from portuguese-empire. Until now both dossiers drew the same 221 cells in 1641-1645 and the size rule gave them to the Dutch, which is right; the event makes it explicit. [fx-36 H31, 1 Nov 2026, from fx-22's handoff]

region.text: the 221 Maranhão cells of Cliopatria's New Netherland 1642 shape: the captaincy of Maranhão with São Luís

ledger.note: 1645: the Dutch abandon São Luís. 'In 1645, most of Dutch Brazil revolted under the leadership of João Fernandes Vieira ... Still in that year, the Dutch abandoned São Luís' (Dutch–Portuguese War page; the Dutch Brazil page dates the capture, 1641, and gives no date for the withdrawal). The cells return to this state. Counterpart: dutch-brazil /ledger/5 books the same cells as a loss to portuguese-empire and the compiler applies it first (dossiers in slug order), so the cells are portuguese-empire's when this gain runs; a gain with counterpart dutch-brazil would find nothing to take and leave them with portuguese-empire until the 1654 keyframe. [fx-36 H31, 1 Nov 2026, from fx-22's handoff, which proposed dutch-brazil as counterpart]

region.text: Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire shape of 1670 inside the Grao-Para region

ledger.note: 1654: the state is reconstituted as Maranhao and Grao-Para.

1737: Belem is formally made the capital. 'Belem became the governors' operational base after the 1670s and was formally made the state capital in 1737' (the same page says the capital moved from Sao Luis in 1751).

intersect.text: the Amazon country of the State of Maranhao, which 'encompassed a large part of the Amazon rainforest'

region.text: Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire shape of 1752 inside the Grao-Para region

ledger.note: 1750 (13 January): the Treaty of Madrid gives Portugal 'most of the Amazon basin'. The page names the basin, not the state: the gain is placed with the State of Maranhao as the only Portuguese state in the Amazon, the researcher's reading; Cliopatria's Portuguese shape jumps by 1.1 M km2 in the region in 1752.

1751 (31 July): Pombal renames the state. The State of Grao-Para and Maranhao 'was created on 31 July 1751 by order of Sebastiao Jose de Carvalho e Melo, 1st Marquis of Pombal' from the State of Maranhao, 'to stimulate economic activities'; Para, 'raised to a unified state with Maranhao', gave its name; Belem is the capital.

1772: the state is split in two. It was 'split in that year into the State of Grao-Para and Rio Negro and the State of Maranhao and Piaui'; both are kept in this dossier until their unification with Brazil in 1775 (the split does not move the outer border).

intersect.text: the Amazon country of the State of Maranhao, which 'encompassed a large part of the Amazon rainforest'

region.text: Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire shape of 1752 inside the Grao-Para region

ledger.note: 1775: the northern states are united with Brazil. 'In 1775 the states were unified under Rio de Janeiro.' The State of Grao-Para and Maranhao page ends the state in 1772 with the split; the Colonial Brazil page gives the 1775 union.

certainty.note: An Amazonian claim with a few forts and mission towns; no surveyed frontier.
The boundary with Spanish America follows the Madeira, Guapore and Javary rivers on paper (Madrid 1750) but was unsurveyed.

notes:
Written by am-06-x from four pages (budget 2-5). Not settled:
(1) Area: no page gives one. Shapes are Cliopatria's Portuguese Empire inside the gazetteer's Grao-Para region (204,000 km2 in 1640 to 1.5 M km2 in 1752). The French at Sao Luis (France Equinoxiale, 1612-1614, Colonial Brazil page), the founding of Belem (1616), the Dutch at Sao Luis (1641-1645; since fx-36 the 221 Maranhao cells of Cliopatria's New Netherland 1642 shape are booked as a loss to dutch-brazil in 1641 and a gain in 1645, ledger 1 and 2) and the Jesuit missions are not on the Maranhao pages and are not drawn; Ceara (detached, undated) and Piaui and Rio Negro are not placed.
(2) Dates differ: capital to Belem 1737 (formal) or 1751 (the same page); end 1772 (State of Grao-Para and Maranhao page, the split) or 1775 (Colonial Brazil, the unification); the dossier runs to 1775 and keeps the two successor states of 1772 (Grao-Para and Rio Negro; Maranhao and Piaui) inside it. If they should be dossiers, their land is: the Rio Negro and Para side vs Maranhao and Piaui.
(3) The 1750 Amazon gain is attributed to this state by the researcher's reading; the Colonial Brazil dossier (this batch) records the Goias, Mato Grosso and Rio Grande do Sul part of the same treaty. Cliopatria's 1778 jump in the region (to 2.8 M km2) falls after this state's end and is left to colonial-brazil.
(4) Counterparts: 'colonial-brazil' (this batch), 'portuguese-empire' (am-06-a), 'spanish-empire' (am-06-b).
